studies.Reference: Case-control study of urinary bladder cancer in metropolitan Nagoya.
studies.Title: Case-control study of urinary bladder cancer in metropolitan Nagoya.
studies.Authors: Ohno Y, Aoki K, Obata K, Morrison AS
studies.comparison_type: Cocoa drinkers vs non-drinkers in males (relative risk reported as significant, value not given)

sample_size.excerpt: The analysis, based on 293 patients and 589 controls who were frequency matched for age, sex, and residence, provided the following major findings.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 293 + 589 = 882

cases.excerpt: The incidence rates of bladder cancer were 2.42 and 7.05/100,000 for females and males, respectively. The analysis, based on 293 patients and 589 controls who were frequency matched for age, sex, and residence, provided the following major findings.

effect_size.excerpt: Significant relative risk was also found in males who drank cocoa.

comparison.excerpt: Significant relative risk was also found in males who drank cocoa.

design.excerpt: We conducted a population-based case-control study of patients with bladder cancer

continent.excerpt: Case-control study of urinary bladder cancer in metropolitan Nagoya.

ethnicity.excerpt: controls drawn randomly from the general population of Metropolitan Nagoya

gender.excerpt: Significant relative risk was also found in males who drank cocoa.
